etymology: English: the hem of the top-of-ticket coat, which every down-ballot candidate rides.
effect: Carries the down-ballot races along on the top of the ticket, and lends a margin to people the voter never met.
tell: A state legislator whose ads feature somebody else's name, and a victory speech that says "we" about a race the speaker did not run.
expires: The first midterm, when the coat is not on the ballot and the hem has to stand up on its own.

confused_with.tell: The honeymoan is grace granted to the winner; the coattails are the margin the winner lends to everyone standing behind them.

senses: The down-ballot pull of a strong top-of-ticket candidate: when the presidential margin is large, legislators, sheriffs, and ballot measures ride the same wave, whether or not the wave was about them.

It works because most voters do not finish the ballot. They pick a top and stop, and the stopping point is the gift - which is why a legislature can swing wildly without a single district changing its mind.
example: *"She won by nine, and the **coattails** carried a county clerk who had run on a road-repair budget and never mentioned the president once."*
